evidence: Nestled within the heart of Hanoi’s Old Quarter, Hang Hom Street stands as a testament to the city’s rich cultural heritage, its narrow lanes lined with traditional “nhà ống” houses, each bearing the marks of time through their tilted tile roofs and weathered facades. This quaint street, known in Vietnamese as Phố Hàng Hòm, has a storied past that dates back to the 19th century when skilled artisans from Ha Vi village migrated to Thang Long, now Hanoi, to establish their craft of making wooden chests and lacquered boxes.
